extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent practitioners, and applicants (pro se and represented)
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of revisions to the Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) reflecting rulemaking, case law, and procedural updates affecting US patent prosecution and examination. Used to guide examination practice, applicant filings, petition practice, and related procedural compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to or copies of a provisional application
rubrics_metrics.description: Process for obtaining access to or copies of a provisional application (Chapter 100 revised).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised to review the process for obtaining access to or copies of a provisional application and to incorporate changes resulting from the ePCT final rule (Facilitating the Use of WIPO's ePCT System). See updated cross-references and contact points (Patent Center, AAU, Certified Copy Center).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship change after restriction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential need to change inventorship after a restriction requirement and that inventorship overlap necessary for a divisional application still exists after an inventorship change (Chapter 200).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added paragraphs discussing when inventorship should be changed following a restriction requirement and clarifying effects on divisional/continuation applications and overlap under 35 U.S.C. 120/121.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for delayed benefit claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and petition practice for making a delayed benefit claim (Chapter 200).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarified that a delayed benefit claim filed more than two years after it was due requires additional explanation of the circumstances surrounding the delay; discussed when petitions under 37 CFR 1.78(b) and 1.78(c) must be filed together; added citation to case law and MPEP cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: English translation of foreign priority applications
rubrics_metrics.description: English language translation of a non-English foreign priority application must be of the certified copy as filed (Chapter 200).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised text to state the English translation must correspond to the certified copy and added discussion summarizing translation requirements and related form paragraph updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merits of a priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: The merits of a priority claim are not determined by the Office unless required for patentability reasons (Chapter 200).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarified that entitlement to a foreign filing date based on disclosure is not determined unless necessary for patentability; staff may not automatically adjudicate merits absent such need.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to suggest pro se applicants obtain representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how and when to suggest that a pro se applicant may wish to employ a registered patent practitioner (Chapter 400).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised to provide additional explanation and examples about when an examiner or USPTO staff should suggest representation to pro se applicants and the manner of such suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules on representation and practitioner conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated reproduced text and discussion of 37 CFR parts addressing representation (e.g., 11.9, 11.10, 11.18) (Chapter 400).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions reflect recent rule changes to rules on practicing before the Office; practitioners should follow updated regulatory language and interpretations in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic communication policies (email and video conferencing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated email and video conference communication policies and permitted communications (Chapter 500 and elsewhere).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarified types of communications that may and may not be submitted via email; video conferences must originate from USPTO links and applicant-provided links are not permitted; references to the Legal Framework for Patent Electronic System should be consulted for current permitted communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small and micro entity status requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifications to requirements for claiming small or micro entity status (Chapter 500).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated criteria for determining micro-entity status (including institution-of-higher-education basis limitations) and the situations that do not constitute a license under 37 CFR 1.27(a)(1); guidance on application filing limits for micro-entity status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and format requirements for sequence listings (ST.25/ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation of ST.25 and ST.26 rulemaking: requirements for electronic submission of sequence listings and XML format for applications filed on/after July 1, 2022 (Chapters 600, 2200, 2400, 1100, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised sections to implement ST.25/ST.26, specify when 'Sequence Listing' vs 'Sequence Listing XML' applies, cross-references to biotech chapters, and instructions for electronic submission via USPTO systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) content and timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Content and timing requirements for an IDS and examiner handling of IDSs (Chapter 600/609).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An IDS may be filed using PTO/SB/08; when no page numbers are supplied, all pages are considered relevant; a bona fide attempt that omits some required content may be allowed time to comply; IDSs filed after certain actions must meet 37 CFR 1.97(d) requirements; late IDSs may be handled as a 'Printer Rush' per MPEP §1309.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of large tables and computer program listing appendices
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and procedures for ASCII/plain text submissions of large tables and requirements for a 'Computer Program Listing Appendix' (Chapter 600).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections revised to address handling of lengthy tables, ASCII submissions, and cross-references to chapter 2400 for sequence listing issues; non-electronic filing fees may apply for paper submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS timing exceptions for weekend/holiday deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: If the last day to file an IDS falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday, the IDS may be timely filed on the next succeeding business day (Chapter 600/609).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarified timing rules for 37 CFR 1.97(b)/(e) and related extensions to next business day where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE practice and processing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified Request for Continued Examination (RCE) practice, including processing checks and limitations (Chapter 700).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must verify that a compliant inventor’s oath or declaration for each inventor was submitted prior to or with the RCE for national stage applications under 35 U.S.C. 371; RCEs will not be processed while the application is undergoing Federal Circuit or district court review; examples of permissible suspension of action and what constitutes good and sufficient cause added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of RCE to switch inventions prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants cannot use an RCE to switch inventions as a matter of right (Chapter 700).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added note and cross-references to 37 CFR 1.145 and MPEP §706.07(h) that an RCE is not a vehicle for changing the invention claimed as a matter of right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review of prior search thoroughness
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner should review the search of a previous examiner to ensure the search is thorough and complete (Chapter 700/904 cross-reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added cross reference to MPEP §904.02 and explicit direction that examiners evaluate prior searches and ensure completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious burden requirement for restriction practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified the 'serious burden' requirement when making a restriction requirement (Chapter 800).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance updated to clarify when a restriction imposes a serious burden on the applicant and how to analyze and document that determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting analysis and patent-term considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated double patenting guidance to include consideration of the patent term filing date and analysis when prior art is excepted under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) or disqualified under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) (Chapter 800).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarified telephone restriction practice, added form paragraph 8.23.03, clarified that only inventions claimed in a divisional may potentially be subject to prohibition under 35 U.S.C. 121, and guidance for claims added after an office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of 'thorough' and 'complete' search and classification procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Added definitions of thorough and complete search and revised classification, routing, and classification challenge procedures in CPC (Chapter 900).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New MPEP §§909.01 and 909.02 replace prior §903.08 material; details classification and routing practices and how to challenge classification in CPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpublication request guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified when a nonpublication request is appropriate (Chapter 1100).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions address timing and effects of nonpublication requests and incorporate ST.25/ST.26 related cross-references and PCT considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal practice clarifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified appellant’s waiver of challenges, Pre-Appeal Brief Request for Review, timing/authorization of appeal forwarding fee, and filing an RCE after a Board decision including a new ground (Chapter 1200).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added guidance on consequences of waiver, Pre-Appeal processes, limits and timing for appeal forwarding fees, and procedures for RCE filing after Board decisions that include new grounds of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for continuation before court mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants wanting to continue prosecution in applications where all claims are rejected and after a decision by the Federal Circuit must file a continuation prior to the court mandate (Chapter 1200).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarified timing obligations for filing continuation applications to preserve prosecution options after an appellate decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of examiner’s amendment and time extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should determine if an extension of time is required for entry of an examiner’s amendment (Chapter 1300).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added clarification and process guidance for deciding when an extension of time must be granted for entry of examiner’s amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal from issue after payment of issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated procedures for withdrawal from issue at the initiative of the Office after payment of the issue fee (Chapter 1300).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarified the process and circumstances under which the Office may withdraw an application from issue after the issue fee is paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printer Rush handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified procedure for handling an application as a 'Printer Rush' (Chapter 1300).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added guidance on how IDSs or other late submissions that affect patentability are handled when an examiner has reached a final determination and a 'Printer Rush' procedure applies (see MPEP §1309.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue oath/declaration signature requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reissue oath or declaration must be signed by a party authorized to act on behalf of the assignee of the entire interest (Chapter 1400).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarified signature requirements and who is authorized to sign reissue oaths/declarations and related reissue filing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of clerical mistakes and recording corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for correction of clerical mistakes, assignee names, named inventors, and benefit claims (Chapter 1400).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated processes and cross-references for correcting clerical matters, recording assignee/inventor name changes, and making benefit claim corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimers and patent term filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated guidance on disclaimers to include consideration of the patent term filing date (Chapter 1400).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised discussion to consider the patent term filing date in disclaimer practice and related form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design claim scope and disclosure sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Design claims are limited to the article of manufacture identified in the claim and do not cover designs in the abstract; when a single plan or planar-view may be sufficient to comply with 35 U.S.C. 112 (Chapter 1500).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added court decision guidance and clarified when a single planar view or plan may suffice for a design claim under 112; updated form paragraphs and emphasis that claims must identify the article of manufacture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer not sufficient to reply to nonstatutory double patenting rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a terminal disclaimer by itself is not a complete reply to a nonstatutory double patenting rejection (Chapter 1500).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 15.24.06 updated to clarify that terminal disclaimer filing may not fully resolve a nonstatutory double patenting objection and additional reply steps may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT national stage timing and amendment practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified time periods and procedures for amending an application after entering the U.S. national stage under the PCT and other PCT-related procedural points (Chapter 1800).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated to reflect PCT rule changes and Administrative Instructions (including PCT Rule 4.11 and Rule 66.8) and clarified when inventor oaths/declarations must be filed relative to RCEs and national stage filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of disclosure and reasonable inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated guidance reflecting rulemaking on the duty of disclosure and reasonable inquiry during examination, reexamination, reissue, and PTAB proceedings (Chapter 2000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporates changes from rulemaking addressing duties of disclosure, specifying obligations and expectations for applicants and practitioners during various proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of prophetic and working examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on properly presenting prophetic and working examples in a patent application (Chapter 2000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised text to incorporate rulemaking changes and provide clear expectations for how prophetic and working examples should be presented to support enablement and written description.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA definitions of applicant and inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation of AIA definitions of 'applicant' and 'inventor' including clarification that a joint inventor must be a natural person (Chapter 2100).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text revised to reflect statutory definitions and updated wording throughout the MPEP (e.g., 'inventor derived the invention' wording changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description, enablement, definiteness, and means-plus-function guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation of court decisions clarifying prior art availability, written description, enablement, definiteness, means-or-step-plus-function limitations, and claim interpretation during prosecution (Chapter 2100).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added case law citations and clarifying discussion on how examiners should apply these doctrines during prosecution, including anticipation in genus-species contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness analysis guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified obviousness analysis including official notice, reasonable expectation of success, and consideration of analogous prior art (Chapter 2100).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated guidance on when to take official notice, how to evaluate reasonable expectation of success, and how to determine analogous art in obviousness rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.130 use
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified the use of affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.130 (Chapter 2100).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added guidance on when and how affidavits/declarations may be used to traverse rejections, including interplay with written description and enablement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing, large table and program listing submission cross-references
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-references among MPEP chapters (600, 2200, 2400) for submission of sequence listings, large tables, and computer program listing appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapters revised to point to each other for biotechnology/sequence listing topics and to specify correct form numbers and submission formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity status discounts and delayed maintenance fee acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified that preamble text before subsection I of §2550 applies generally to entity status discounts and requirements for acceptance of delayed payment of a maintenance fee in an expired patent consistent with petition practice (Chapter 2500).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reorganization clarifies when discounts apply and how delayed maintenance fee payments are evaluated under relevant petitions and procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) determination and reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions to explain PTA reductions in view of Federal Circuit decisions (e.g., Supernus) and to clarify what constitutes a notification under 35 U.S.C. 132 (Chapter 2700).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated the reproduced text of 37 CFR 1.704 and associated discussion, added new paragraphs to analyze consequences of court decisions (Supernus, Biogen) and clarified use of original patent grant date for calculating extensions for reissued patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: International design (Hague) application practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified flow, direct/indirect filing, representative appointment, correspondence address, inventor identity (natural person), title/description/drawings requirements, foreign priority claims, corrections, and recording of changes for Hague design applications (Chapter 2900).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added detail on indirect filing via USPTO, requirement/benefit of using official forms (DM/1), eHague references, timing/control of publication, optional content items, drawing/figure requirements, and updated fees/online fee calculator guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording changes and corrections under Hague Rules and Articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for making Rule 22 corrections and recording changes under Hague Article 16, and what is recorded in the International Bureau (Chapter 2900).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added subsections on corrections under Rule 22 and recording of ownership or representation changes under Article 16, and clarified effect and timing for entries and corrected filing receipts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph updates and organization (Chapter FPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter FPC consolidates form paragraphs, indicating revisions, deletions, and additions and providing cross-references to numbered MPEP chapters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Subject Matter Index to locate sections where a given form paragraph is reproduced; revised form paragraphs are consolidated in Chapter FPC for reference.
